messages:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 streaming latency breach in prod-us-west-1 (> 3s) — threshold trip at 07:41 UTC. impact: degraded streaming responses and stalls. auto-run checks kicked off.

sam: ack, oncall here. seeing alert on pager duty. grabbing dashboards.

alex: looking at trace sampler — p50 fine, p95 ~1.1s, p99 spiking to 4-7s for streaming endpoints. tails concentrated on nodes gpu-pool-usw-12.

jess: logs show repeated `KVCache::miss` and `cuda` stalls around same window. throwing `ECC correctable` noise on node 12.

maria: running quick psql to check request distribution — ~12% of streaming requests routed to that pool last 10m.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) remove node from rotation, 2) enable fallback routing to warm-pool, 3) roll streaming requests to quantized variant for affected hosts if needed.

devon: +1. I'll run the drain. kubectl cordon and drain planned on node gpu-pool-usw-12.

ops-bot: command executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12.prod.usw` (ok)

ops-bot: command executed: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12.prod.usw --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (ok)

alex: routing flip started — updating API routing policy to prefer warm-pool for short tail requests. config snippet:
```
route_policy: |
  if latency_estimate > 1500ms then prefer warm-pool
  fallback: quantized-variant
```

jess: also bumping streaming timeout from 25s -> 20s to fail fast for backpressure.

maria: checking GPU telemetry for node 12: memory ECC correctables spiked ~3000/minute for 07:39-07:43. thermal sensor jumped 10C above baseline. fan RPM oscillating.

sam: so this looks like intermittent ECC + thermal causing stalls — likely hardware degrading. escalate to hardware team and isolate node.

devon: opened ticket HW-2026 with datacenter ops. attaching logs.

alex: running quick KV cache warm up on warm-pool to reduce cold misses while routing shift completes.

jess: load now stable for warm-pool. p99 trending back down to ~1.2s. p95 0.9s.

incident-bot: Incident update: customer-facing SLO breach window approx 07:39-07:52 UTC. estimated affected requests: 9.8% of streaming volume in us-west-1. No error-rate spike, primarily tail latency.

maria: I'm drafting a one-liner for customer comms: "We investigated a brief spike in streaming latency in US-West due to a degraded GPU node; traffic was routed to fallback capacity and service performance recovered. We're replacing the affected hardware and will report back with RCA." Thoughts?

sam: good. add estimated customer impact numbers: ~10% requests experienced > p99 threshold, median unaffected.

alex: added diagnostics to capture ECC counts on warm-pool while hardware ticket progresses. Also enabling longer retention for traces of that window.

devon: datacenter ops confirm node has repeated correctable ECC and fan controller reports 'oscillation'. plan: take node offline for burn-in and diagnostics, possibly RMA.

jess: follow-up tasks: 1) mark node as quarantined in inventory, 2) schedule removal from GPU pool, 3) verify no further residual tail after warm pool routing removed.

ops-bot: action logged: `incident-7432108765`: participants assigned [sam, alex, devon, jess].

sam: quick customer impact calc: during 13-minute window, 9.8% of streaming sessions saw p99 > 3s. downstream clients using streaming may have experienced stalls but no data corruption.

maria: flagged in status page draft.

alex: next steps timeline: 1) hardware RMA start in 2 hours, 2) follow-up RCA in 48 hours, 3) quantized fallback policy review to reduce blast radius.

sam: closing live mitigation — routing rollback to normal will wait until node removed and warm-pool health validated.

jess: final note — add a synthetic that specifically exercises KV cache warm path to catch this earlier next time. filing task INF-912.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: live mitigation successful, p99 returned to SLO within 12 minutes of mitigation start. Postmortem assigned.

sam: thanks all. adding timeline notes to postmortem doc and will ping for RCA draft. :thumbsup:
